clue.text: Agonises over missing son, and gets protection

indicators.note: 'over' signals the letters of the first word are worked over and rearranged, with 'missing' showing the next word's letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters
taken as written, the letters to be removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone worrying about the absence of their son, who nonetheless finds a safe haven.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: AGONISES holds the letters of SON plus those of the answer, so remove S, O and N and rearrange what remains (A, G, I, E, S).
explanation.definitionFit: An aegis is a shield or sponsorship, so it is a form of cover or safeguarding.

clue.text: Spring time?

parts.note: read 'spring' as a jump rather than the season: a calendar period named after a bound, with an extra day in February

explanation.definitionFit: The calendar year with 29 February is named for a jump, and 'spring' is another word for jump.

clue.text: Friend gets up to chase pet

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word for friend is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pal is a casual word for a friend
to dog someone is to follow or chase them

explanation.surface: A friend rises to go after a pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' is the reversal signal, reading upward in this down clue; 'to chase' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered dog kept as a companion, a household pet.

clue.text: Spell "designate"

definitions.meaning: a spell is a period of time, such as a school or office stint
to designate is to name or call something

explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed period (a spell), and to term something is to name or designate it.

clue.text: Watch, or desperation seizes the assembled throngs

indicators.note: the phrase 'Watch, or desperation' seizes, that is holds within it, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A warning to look out because despair is grabbing the gathered crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across watcH OR DESperation, held by 'seizes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are large crowds of people gathered together, the same as throngs.

clue.text: The fleet docked with sick old animal

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter of the word for fleet is cut off

parts.note: the Armada was the Spanish fleet, and an armada is any fleet of warships
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A naval fleet in port alongside an ailing aged creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' trims the final A from ARMADA to leave ARMAD; 'docked' looks like ships tying up in harbour, but it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured South American mammal, so an animal.

clue.text: Representatives' attendance in Leeds match

indicators.note: the word for attendance goes in the middle of the rearranged letters
the letters of the city name are matched up in a different order

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators attending a sports event

explanation.surface: Football-speak: how many turned up to watch a Leeds game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like the football fixture but rearranges the city's letters, and 'in' sets the attendance word inside them. The possessive in the definition reads as 'representatives is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Delegates are people sent to speak or vote on behalf of others, so they are representatives.

clue.text: Romance in the play ground

definitions.meaning: to romance someone is to woo them
a ground for play, such as one marked out for tennis or squash

explanation.surface: A love story in a school playground or on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To court is to woo, and a court is also an area marked out for games like tennis.

clue.text: Former worker admits time is still standing

indicators.note: the former worker lets the abbreviation for time in among his letters

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An ex-employee confesses that the clock is not moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' lets the time letter into the middle of the charade, just after the X.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means surviving or existing, like a document that remains in existence today.

clue.text: Transparent hat worn by one member

indicators.note: a hat is worn over a head, so the word for hat goes round the other pieces

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A see-through cap on a lone politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' looks like it describes a hat on a head; here it means the hat word goes round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is perfectly clear, so you can see through it.

clue.text: Variety provided in game shot?

definitions.meaning: the haul of assorted birds a shooting party brings home

explanation.surface: An assortment supplied by a day's shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed bag is a diverse assortment, literally a hunter's haul of several species.

clue.text: Churchman's right on the brink

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in an across clue the letter for right is placed on, that is after, the word for brink

parts.note: a verge is an edge or brink

explanation.surface: A clergyman's politics lean rightward, close to the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets R after VERGE. A verger is a lay church officer who looks after the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is a church officer who carries the rod before clergy and tends the building.

clue.text: Settle origins of riots over open season thus

indicators.note: the origin of each word is where it begins, its first letter

explanation.surface: Calming the starts of disturbances once the open season ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the last five words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they settle for the night on a perch.

clue.text: Sailor lies about descent

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: the letters of the word lies are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaman lying about how he came down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal, though the surface reads it as 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a cliff face on a rope, so the noun names a descent.

clue.text: Prepare too hard for open rule, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the words for open and rule are heard rather than written

parts.note: open is overt and rule is reign, together said as one phrase

explanation.surface: An athlete getting ready with excessive effort for an open regime.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERT (open) + REIGN (rule) said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise or practise beyond what is useful, like an athlete preparing too intensively.

clue.text: Find out disc is missing — and finished

indicators.note: the word disc is missing from the word for find out, so remove it

parts.note: to discover is to find out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discover that a record has gone and it's all ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DISC from the front of DISCOVER and four letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it is completed or at an end.

clue.text: Figurehead is the type to accept the end of war

indicators.note: the word for type takes in the following letter, accepting it inside

parts.note: a font is a set of type in one style

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A leader is the sort who will welcome peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' war gives R, and 'to accept' puts it inside FONT after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: A front is a public face masking who really holds control, as a figurehead does.

clue.text: Foot admitted spots were most weird

indicators.note: the abbreviation for foot lets in, that is admits, the word for spots

parts.note: to spot is to see, and to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A footman confessed that blemishes were particularly strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' is the container signal; 'spots' reads as blemishes but here is the verb meaning sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Fey means otherworldly or strange, so feyest is the superlative of weird.

clue.text: Plain fruit, we hear

indicators.note: the words signal that the fruit name is heard, sounding like the answer

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo

explanation.surface: Simple fruit, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: The ugli fruit is a wrinkly Jamaican citrus; said aloud it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain is a polite word for unattractive in appearance.

clue.text: Change it, or rule is not made apparent

indicators.note: the instruction to change the following words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter something, or a regulation that stays concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges the letters of IT OR RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is hidden, kept beneath the surface rather than openly stated.

clue.text: It's gruesome to bear, say

indicators.note: signals that the word for bear is spoken, giving a similar-sounding word

parts.note: the grizzly is a large North American brown bear

explanation.surface: Something horrible to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the verb 'endure', but it is the animal, the grizzly.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly means horrifying, causing revulsion, just like gruesome.

clue.text: Horses for rent — on board ship?

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting within it, so the word for rent goes inside

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: Animals available to rent, perhaps carried on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the container signal: what is on board a ship is inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shires are heavy draught horses, a large breed originally from the English Midlands.

clue.text: Thomas has a temperature? Nothing but fruit

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Thomas has a fever? He eats only fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces in order give TOM + A + T + O.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a berry, so it counts as a fruit.

clue.text: Demented artist started sleeping in the city

parts.note: mad means demented
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: the word sleeping is started, giving only its first letter

explanation.surface: A crazed painter dozed off in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' takes S from sleeping; MADRAS is the former name of Chennai, in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Madras, now Chennai, is a major Indian city on the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Look around home of banker

indicators.note: the word for look goes around the word for home

parts.note: to see is to look
in means at home

explanation.surface: Glancing round a financier's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal. A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks; here the river through Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so in crossword terms it is a banker, and the Seine flows through Paris.

clue.text: Exchange rate isn't a thing to be played with

definitions.text: a thing to be played with

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that the exchange rate is not something to toy with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' rearranges RATE ISNT; 'Exchange rate' reads as finance.
explanation.definitionFit: A model railway set is a toy, something children play with.

clue.text: Spoke of link with eastern language

indicators.note: a word spoken aloud, so the word for link is heard

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: Talked about a connection to an Asian tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE said aloud gives the answer; 'with' joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official language of Thailand in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Laments expressing desires to chase deputy head

indicators.note: expressing means saying aloud, so the built words are heard

parts.note: desires are urges, chasing the head letter of deputy, D: say them together

explanation.surface: Complaints voicing ambitions to pursue the deputy headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: D (deputy head) followed by URGES (desires), said as one word, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, a lament.

clue.text: Worked topless and got drunk

indicators.note: without its top, the word for worked loses its first letter

parts.note: toiled means worked hard

explanation.surface: Laboured with no shirt on and became tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the T from TOILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is British slang for tipsy or intoxicated.

clue.text: Even a horse is of the utmost importance

parts.note: par means level or even, as in on a par
a mount is a horse to ride

explanation.surface: Even a horse matters greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces in order: PAR + A + MOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, more important than anything else.
